ov: Four species of tiny antelope living in the bushlands of eastern and south-western Africa. Pairs stay together for life in small territories, which they mark with scent from a gland under each eye. They get almost all their water from food and rarely need to drink.

why.et: Hunted locally, mostly with snares, for its hide and bones.

rg: Bushlands of eastern Africa, plus a separate population of Kirk's dik-dik in Namibia and south-west Africa.
df: Leaves, shoots, fruit and berries, with little or no grass.
fx: Unlike other ruminants, which are born forefeet first, a dik-dik is born nose first.
Its long, flexible snout works like bellows, cooling blood with evaporation in extreme heat.
